questions.question: The average of 45 numbers was found to be 39. Later on, it was detected that a number 65 was misread as 56. Find the correct average of the given numbers.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average of 45 numbers = 39

Number 65 was misread as = 56

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of elements/number of elements

**Calculation:**

⇒ The sum of 45 numbers = 39 × 45 = 1755

⇒ Now, misread 65 = 1755 - 56 =1699

⇒ Real number = 1699 + 65 = 1764

⇒ Correct average = 1764/45= 39.2

**∴ The correct answer is 39.2**

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 16 hours, respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage at the bottom, it takes 90 minutes more to fill the cistern. How much time will the leakage take to empty the completely filled tank?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time is taken by pipe A to fill tank = 12 hours

Time is taken by pipe B to fill tank = 16 hours

Formula used:

Time = Total work/efficiency

Calculation:

Here, extra 90 minutes represents the extra time taken by the pipes due to the leak.

Total units of water to be filled = LCM of (12, 16) = 48 units.

Pipe A can fill 4 units of water in 1 hr.

Pipe B can fill 3 units of water in 1 hr.

Normal time taken to fill the tank = 48/7 hrs = 6(6/7) hrs.

With 90 min extra, the pipes would take (48/7 + 3/2) hr to fill the tank.

Let the leakage can empty N units of water in 1 hr.

⇒ (4 + 3 - N) × (48/7 + 3/2) = 48

⇒ (7 - N) × 117/14 = 48

 ⇒117N = 819 - 672

⇒ N = 147/117

Leakage can empty 1 units of water in 117/147 hr.

Leakage can empty 48 units of water in 117/147 × 48 = 5616/147

⇒ 1872/49 = 38 (10)/(49) hr

∴ Time taken to empty the tank is 38 (10)/(49) hrs.

questions.question: An inlet pipe can fill an empty tank in 3.6 hours, while an outlet pipe can drain a completely-filled tank in 6.3 hours. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously when the tank is empty, in how many hours will the tank get completely filled?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

An inlet pipe fills tank in = 3.6 hours

Outlet pipe drains tank in = 6.3 hours

**Solution:**

Rate of inlet pipe = 1 / 3.6 Rate of outlet pipe = 1 / 6.3

Net rate when both are open = 1 / 3.6 - 1 / 6.3

Find the LCM of 36 and 63 to simplify the calculation, which is 252.

Net rate = (70/252) - (40/252) = 30/252 = 5/42

Time to fill the tank when both pipes are open = 1 / Net rate = 42 / 5

**Time to fill tank = 8.4 hours**

questions.question: The average weight of 49 students is 53 kg. When a new student is admitted to the class, the average decreases by 500 g. Find the weight of the new student.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of 49 students = 53 kg

When a new student is admitted (now 50 students), the average decreases by 500 g = 0.5 kg

New average = 53 kg - 0.5 kg = 52.5 kg

**Formula used:**

Total weight = Average weight × Number of students

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 49 students = 53 × 49

Total weight with 50 students = 52.5 × 50

Weight of the new student = Total weight with 50 students - Total weight of 49 students

⇒ 53 × 49 = 2597 kg

⇒ 52.5 × 50 = 2625 kg

**Weight of the new student = 2625 kg - 2597 kg = 28 kg**

questions.question: Ronak and Riya can do a work in 12 and 18 days, respectively. They worked together for six days and then Ronak left. Find the time taken by Riya to complete the remaining work.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.

Ronak's efficiency = 3, Riya's efficiency = 2.

Work done together in 6 days = (3 + 2) × 6 = 30 units.

Remaining work = 36 − 30 = 6 units.

Time for Riya = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Ronak = 12 days

Time taken by Riya = 18 days

Working together period = 6 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Combined efficiency of Ronak + Riya = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work done in 6 days = Combined efficiency × Number of days

⇒ Work done = 5 × 6 = 30 units

⇒ Remaining work = Total work − Work done

⇒ Remaining work = 36 − 30 = 6 units

Total Work Concept

Total work is always considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual time taken by each person to simplify efficiency calculations.

Efficiency Inversion

If two people A and B can do a work in x and y days, the ratio of their efficiencies is y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

This logic is identical to inlet pipes filling a tank, where work done is the volume of the tank and efficiency is the rate of flow.</p

questions.question: The average score in an English exam of a class of 45 students in a coaching centre is 52. A group of 6 boys having an average score of 40 leave the class and another group of eight boys having an average score of 43 join the class. What is the new average score of the class?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The total number of students in the coaching centre is 45

The average score of 45 students is 52.

The number of students leaving the coaching centre is 6.

The average of students leaving class is 40.

The number of students joining the coaching centre is 8

The average score of 8 boys joining the class is 43.

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum of all the scores of the students / No. of students

**Calculation:**

Sum of the scores of all the 45 students = Average × No. of students = 52 × 45 = 2340

A group of 6 boys leaving the class, average score is 40

Sum of the scores of 6 boys = Average × No. of students = 40 × 6 = 240

Sum of the scores of 8 boys joining the class = Average × No. of students = 43 × 8 = 344

Average score of the class = ([Sum of the scores of all the 45 students - Sum of the scores of 6 boys leaving the class + Sum of the scores of 8 boys joining the class] )/([Total number of students - No. of students leaving + No. of students joining the class])

Average score of the class = ([2340 - 240 + 344])/([45 - 6 + 8])

Average score of the class = (2444 )/( 47) = 52

Hence, the average score of the class is 52.

questions.question: In what proportion should a grocer mix wheat at ₹12 per kg and ₹25 per kg so as to make a mixture of worth ₹20 per kg?
questions.solution:

Cost of 1st variety = ₹ 12 per kg

Cost of 2nd variety = ₹ 25 per kg

Cost of mixture = ₹ 20 per kg

Calculation:

Let the ratio of 1st variety to 2nd variety be "1 : x"

⇒ 1 × 12 + x × 25 = (1 + x) 20

⇒ 12 + 25x = 20 + 20x

⇒ 25x - 20x = 20 - 12

⇒ 5x = 8

⇒ 5/8 = 1/x

⇒ 5 : 8 = 1 : x

∴ The ratio is 5 : 8.

questions.question: Ramu had to select a list of numbers between 1 and 1000 (including both), which are divisible by both 2 and 7. How many such numbers are there?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ramu had to select numbers between 1 to 1000 ( including both)

which are divisible by both 2 and 7 

**Formula used:**

aₙ = a + ( n - 1) × d 

Where, an = last number, a = 1st term, n = number of terms, d= common difference

d = 2nd term - 1st term = 3rd term - 2nd term = 4th term - 3rd term etc.....

**Calculation:**

Here, it is given a list of numbers between 1 to 1000 (including both) , which are divisible by both 2 and 7

So, to be divisible by both 2 and 7, the number has to be divisible by 14 

As, we know that,

aₙ = a + ( n - 1) × d

So, a = 1st term = 14 , 2nd term = 28 , last term = 994 

d = 2nd term - 1st term = 28 - 14 = 14 

⇒ 994 = 14 + ( n - 1) × 14 

⇒ 980 = 14n - 14 

⇒ 994 = 14n

⇒ n = 71 

**Hence, there are 71 terms between 1 to 1000 (including both ) which are divisible by both 2 and 7.**

**Concept used:**

If two sides are equal, then angles opposite to their sides are also equal 

Sum of the angles in a triangle is 180^circ 

If a side of a triangle is produced , the exterior angle so formed is equal to the 

sum of the two interior opposite angles

⇒ x + x + angleBAC = 180

questions.question: The average weight of 15 people increases by 3.2 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 52 kg. The weight of the new person is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

15 people, average increase = 3.2 kg, replaced person = 52 kg

**Formula:**

New average increase = old total + (new person - replaced person)

**Calculation:**

Total increase = 15 × 3.2 = 48 kg

New person = 52 kg + 48 kg = 100 kg

**The weight of the new person is 100 kg**

questions.question: A mixture of 750 kg of alloy of copper and tin contains 25% tin. How much tin must be added so that it becomes 70% of the mixture?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A mixture of 750 kg of alloy of copper and tin contains 25% tin.

**Formula Used:**

Final percentage of tin = (Initial mass of tin + Added mass of tin) / (Total mass of mixture + Added mass of tin) × 100

**Calculation:**

Initial mass of tin = 25% of 750 kg

Initial mass of tin = 0.25 × 750

Initial mass of tin = 187.5 kg

Let x kg of tin be added.

Final percentage of tin = 70%

Then,

70 = (187.5 + x) / (750 + x) × 100

⇒ 70 / 100 = (187.5 + x) / (750 + x)

⇒ 0.7 = (187.5 + x) / (750 + x)

⇒ 0.7 × (750 + x) = 187.5 + x

⇒ 525 + 0.7x = 187.5 + x

⇒ 525 - 187.5 = x - 0.7x

⇒ 337.5 = 0.3x

⇒ x = 337.5 / 0.3

⇒ x = 1125 kg

**The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Anwesha's marks in a class test of Sanskrit were incorrectly entered as 99 instead of 66. If there are 55 students in the class, then what is the increment in the average marks of the class in Sanskrit because of this typing error?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Anwesha's marks were incorrectly entered as 99 instead of 66.

Number of students in the class = 55

**Concept:**

The increment in the average marks of the class is given by the difference in marks divided by the number of students.

**Formula Used:**

Increment in average marks = (Incorrect marks - Correct marks) / Total number of students

**Calculation:**

⇒ Incorrect marks = 99

⇒ Correct marks = 66

⇒ Number of students = 55

⇒ Difference in marks = 99 - 66 = 33

⇒ Increment in average marks = 33 / 55

⇒ Increment in average marks = 0.6

**∴ The correct answer is option 3.**

questions.question: The average height of three kids is 56 cm and their heights are in the proportion of 7 ∶ 8 ∶ 9. Find the heights of all the three.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average height of 3 kids = 56 cm

Proportion of heights = 7 : 8 : 9

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the height of three kids be 7x, 8x and 9x.

⇒ (7x+8x+9x)/(3) = 56

⇒ (24x)/(3) = 56

⇒ x = (56)/(8) = 7

⇒ Height of first kid = 7 × 7 = 49 cm

⇒ Height of second kid = 8 × 7 = 56 cm

⇒ Height of third kid = 9 × 7 = 63 cm

**Therefore, the heights of three kids are 49 cm, 56 cm and 63 cm respectively.**
